featured_techniques.technique: Cross product viewed as a dual of a linear functional
Determinant expansion with i-hat, j-hat, k-hat to extract dual vector coordinates
Duality: transforming a map to R into dot product with a vector
Constructing a linear functional L(x) = det([x v w]) and solving for P
Geometric interpretation of dual vector: P perpendicular to v and w with magnitude equal to parallelogram area

sections.description: Introduces forming a 3×3 determinant to compute v × w, with v and w as the 2nd and 3rd columns and the unit basis i, j, k in the first column to signal vector coordinates.
sections.title: Cross product computation via determinant and basis vectors

sections.description: Recaps that a linear map from space to the number line corresponds to a unique dual vector so that the transformation equals a dot product with that vector.
sections.title: Duality reminder: linear maps to the real line and their dual vectors

sections.description: Defines a linear functional L on R^3 parameterized by fixed vectors v and w, and asks for a vector P such that L(x) = P · x for all x = (x, y, z).
sections.title: Defining L(x) = det([x v w]) and seeking its dual P

sections.description: Explains how the coefficients that accompany x, y, z in the determinant reveal the coordinates of the dual vector P when treated as a linear functional.
sections.title: Computational route to P via determinant expansion

sections.description: Reminds that in 2D the determinant yields a scalar area, and clarifies that the 3D cross product outputs a vector perpendicular to v and w.
sections.title: 2D cross product intuition and 3D cross product context

sections.description: Makes the first column variable (u, v, w) and shows the determinant defines a linear map from R^3 to R, highlighting linearity and the matrix interpretation.
sections.title: Treating u as a variable: a 3D-to-R functional via determinant

sections.description: Demonstrates that the same P obtained computationally via the determinant corresponds to a vector perpendicular to v and w whose length equals the area of the parallelogram spanned by v and w; orientation matches the right-hand rule.
sections.title: Geometric interpretation: P as the dual vector and the dot-product equality

sections.description: Summarizes how both the computational determinant approach and the geometric interpretation yield the same dual vector, revealing why cross product ties computation to geometry.
sections.title: Synthesis: two perspectives converge to the same dual vector

sections.description: Notes that the next video will introduce change of basis, tying the current ideas back to broader linear algebra concepts.
sections.title: Preview: change of basis and upcoming topics

summary: In this chapter excerpt, 3Blue1Brown unpacks the 3D cross product v × w by viewing it as the dual of a specific linear transformation from three-dimensional space to the real numbers. The talk connects determinant-based computations (via a matrix with v and w as columns and a variable first column) to a linear functional on R^3, then identifies a dual vector P whose dot product with any input vector x, y, z reproduces that determinant. The presentation alternates between a computational route—expanding a determinant and recognizing i-hat, j-hat, k-hat as the coefficients of the resulting vector—and a geometric route—seeing the dual vector as perpendicular to v and w with length equal to the area of the parallelogram spanned by v and w, and using projection arguments. The discussion also situates this within the familiar 2D determinant interpretation (area) and extends to how a single-variable input yields a linear transformation; the dual vector P reconciles the two viewpoints and explains the cross product’s geometric and computational coherence. The video foreshadows a change-of-basis topic as a future direction.
title: Cross products as dual linear functionals: a determinant and duality journey in 3Blue1 Brown’s Essence of Linear Algebra
topics: linear transformation from R^3 to R
3x3 determinant with a variable first column
projection onto a line perpendicular to v and w
matrix representation of a linear functional
